svg.title: TCP vs UDP: reliable conversation or fire-and-forget
svg.desc: Both ride on IP and use ports; TCP adds a handshake, acknowledgements and retransmission, UDP adds almost nothing
svg.text: TCP vs UDP: reliable conversation or fire-and-forget
Both ride on IP and use ports; TCP adds a handshake, acknowledgements and retransmission, UDP adds almost nothing
The application decides: retry (DNS) or skip the
8-byte header, no waiting, works with broadcast
and multicast, perfect for small request/response
HEADERS — HOW MUCH EACH PROTOCOL ADDS
TCP header: 20+ bytes — sequence and ack numbers enable ordering, retransmission and flow control
UDP header: 8 bytes — ports, length, checksum. That's all.
TCP — use when every byte must arrive
UDP — use when speed beats perfection
HTTP/HTTPS · SSH · email · file transfer · databases
DNS · DHCP · VoIP · video calls · online games · QUIC
TCP = SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK, then numbered data with ACKs and retransmits. UDP = just send it.
Neither is 'better': pick reliability (TCP) or low latency (UDP) based on what the application can tolerate losing.
